`max_body_size` is now an option on `Starlette`, `Router`, `Mount` and `Route`, and `RequestBodyLimitMiddleware` is available standalone. The full suite shows 10 failures, all Windows-only: symlink privileges and permissions in `test_staticfiles.py`, and a path regex in `test_config.py::test_missing_env_file_raises`. I didn't re-run the suite without my changes to confirm that. All the new tests in `tests/test_body_limit.py` pass. I couldn't run `ruff` because the sandbox blocked it, so lint and formatting are unchecked.

## What changed

- **Middleware:** it lives in `starlette/middleware/bodylimit.py`.
  - It counts the bytes it actually receives, and rejects with a plain-text `413 Content Too Large`.
  - A `Content-Length` over the limit is rejected before the app is called. A missing or understated header doesn't let a bigger body through.
  - If the app has already started its response when the limit is crossed, no second response is sent and `receive()` raises to stop the body stream.
- **Where it sits in the stack:**
  - `Starlette(max_body_size=…)` puts the middleware just inside `ServerErrorMiddleware` and outside your own middleware.
  - `Router`, `Mount` and `Route` wrap themselves, outside any middleware you give them.
- **Inner limits:** all layers share one per-request counter, so an inner limit replaces the outer one. Because it can raise the limit, an app-level `Content-Length` check is deferred to the first body read whenever something inside the app sets its
